statements.statement: An analog signal can only be on or off, just like a digital signal.
statements.explanation: Unlike digital signals, an analog signal can be any value in a continuous range -- think of a dimmer switch rather than a light switch.

statements.statement: A microcontroller uses an ADC (analog-to-digital converter) to turn analog voltages into numbers your code can use.
statements.explanation: Since microcontrollers work with digital data internally, they need an ADC to convert smoothly varying analog voltages into discrete numeric values.

statements.statement: Every pin on a microcontroller can read analog signals.
statements.explanation: Not all pins support analog input. You need specific ADC-capable pins or an external ADC chip to read analog signals.
